name: What should I ask before hiring an accessible bathroom remodeler?

mainEntity.name: What questions reveal whether a contractor really knows accessible bathroom remodeling instead of just doing generic bathroom updates?
mainEntity.text: What questions reveal whether a contractor really knows accessible bathroom remodeling instead of just doing generic bathroom updates?

acceptedAnswer.text: A contractor who truly understands accessible bathroom remodeling should be able to discuss more than tile and cabinets. Ask how they handle zero-threshold showers, shower slope, drain placement, blocking for grab bars, toilet clearance, and turning radius in compact rooms. They should also be able to explain how they adapt the design for the specific mobility needs of the user, whether that means a walker, wheelchair, age-in-place planning, or post-surgery recovery. In Los Angeles homes, they should be comfortable working with older construction, permits, and the challenges of slab or small-footprint layouts. It helps if they can show examples of previous accessible projects and explain why certain products or layouts were chosen. A strong contractor will discuss tradeoffs clearly, including where accessibility, luxury, and budget may conflict.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask whether they have designed curbless showers, widened doorways, added reinforcement for grab bars, and solved clearance issues in small bathrooms. A qualified remodeler should explain layout, waterproofing, slope, and fixture placement in accessibility terms, not just talk about finishes.
